reason: Conversation 2 covered far more of the real cause: it had the homeowner check the door seal fold and pump filter together, then addressed the slimy dispenser housing and finished with a hot empty maintenance wash, which lines up with the hidden truth (biofilm from seal, drawer and filter, fixed by cleaning plus a hot cycle). Conversation 1 stopped at the drain filter, declared the sludge 'definitely the cause', and ended abruptly without any hot wash, seal, drawer, softener or door-open advice. Conversation 2 is marked down for pushing a 'replacement part' model-number panel when no part was justified and for describing a non-existent condenser mesh flap behind the drawer on this model, which wasted the homeowner's time, but she still found the drawer gunk and got a workable fix. Neither asked about wash temperatures, softener use or leaving the door open, and both correctly said to unplug before opening the filter.
